slot.brief: Given y = αx − βx², compare with the standard parabolic trajectory to extract u, θ and range.

stem: The trajectory of a projectile is given by y = 3x - 4x^2, where x and y are in metre. The horizontal range of the projectile is

verdicts.working: Set y=0: x(3−4x)=0. The nonzero root gives the horizontal range, x=3/4=0.75 m.

working:
Compare with standard form y = x tan(theta) - [g/(2u^2 cos^2 theta)]x^2. Coefficient of x gives tan(theta) = 3. Coefficient of x^2 gives g/(2u^2 cos^2 theta) = 4. Horizontal range R = u^2 sin(2 theta)/g = tan(theta) / [g/(2u^2 cos^2 theta)] = 3/4 = 0.75 m.

Independent check: Set y=0: x(3−4x)=0. The nonzero root gives the horizontal range, x=3/4=0.75 m.
solution:
At the landing point, $y=0$:
$$x(3-4x)=0 \implies x=0,\;\frac{3}{4}.$$
The nonzero root gives the horizontal range, so $R=0.75\,\text{m}$.
